chk_problem.poster_evidence: Dermatology AI models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet are increasingly proposed for settings whose patients differ from the training population along two confounded axes: skin tone and disease distribution. We ask which factor contributes more to the generalization gap and whether failure on unfamiliar diseases reflects merely missing output labels or a genuine representational deficit.

chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Using public data and free-tier compute, we decomposed the dermatology-AI generalization gap. Disease-distribution shift dominated skin tone in the evaluated setting. Cheap adaptation was most effective when the starting representation already encoded the target diseases.
